findings.title: Marketing copy uses opaque technical jargon
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: This sounds like a vague AI claim and does not tell me what inputs are used, how the story is generated, or why the result will actually be good.

findings.title: Hero image has no accessible description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
findings.why: The large image gives no textual indication to assistive technology and appears to be a generic illustration rather than evidence of the actual product.

findings.title: Editing control is deferred behind an FAQ
findings.evidence: [9] button "Can I edit the story?"
findings.why: Whether I can correct or regenerate a problematic page is a key decision criterion, but this is not surfaced in the main workflow.

findings.title: Login fields have no persistent labels
findings.evidence: [5] and [6] are textboxes with no label, using only placeholders "Email" and "Password".
findings.why: Placeholder-only labelling weakens accessibility and makes the fields less robust once text is entered.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The bottom links "Privacy", "Terms", and "Contact" appear extremely faint against the pale background.
findings.why: I can barely read these trust-related links, which matters on a site handling children's photos and personal memories.

findings.title: Raw error code and vague sync warning
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my family profile is incomplete, stale, or safe to use, and that uncertainty is especially unhelpful when I’m about to supply details about my child.

findings.title: Potential profile reliability and privacy uncertainty
findings.evidence: “profile sync incomplete” immediately after logging in
findings.why: Before entering Zara’s details, I need confidence that the site isn’t working from stale or incomplete profile data and isn’t silently duplicating it.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint.
findings.why: I want easy access to the privacy and terms information before sharing my child’s information.

findings.title: Wrong default relationship creates a contradictory character setup
findings.evidence: [11] Relationship is selected as “Grandparent” by default while the adjacent field says [10] “Who else is in the story?”
findings.why: If I fail to notice and change it, the generator will model Dad as a grandparent rather than Zara’s father.

findings.title: No description field for the second character
findings.evidence: [10] “Who else is in the story?” and [11] “Relationship” are the only controls for the second person; there is no appearance field.
findings.why: I need Dad to be a tall man with short hair, a short beard and a grey jumper so he remains recognisable across pages.

findings.title: Footer text and links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer links “Privacy”, “Terms” and “Contact” appear extremely faint against the background.
findings.why: Privacy matters here because this concerns my child’s details, but the relevant link is hard to see and read.

findings.title: Footer navigation has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer labels “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are rendered in extremely faint grey.
findings.why: The privacy link is important given that this flow involves a child’s appearance and family memories, but it is difficult to see or read.

findings.title: Back preserves a corrupted truncated memory
findings.evidence: Textbox [18] still ends with “It matters because it was o” and has no character counter or truncation warning.
findings.why: Returning to correct a field can leave the book prompt subtly wrong without making the loss obvious.

findings.title: Heading does not precisely describe the controls
findings.evidence: “Choose the look & feel”
findings.why: It makes the configuration sound more extensive than the two visible settings.

findings.title: No explanation of Lexile bands for lay users
findings.evidence: “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L”, and “Lexile 800L+”
findings.why: As a technical user I recognise Lexile, but a parent choosing for a seven-year-old should not need decoding knowledge to make the right choice.

findings.title: Story field silently truncates valid input
findings.evidence: The memory box now only shows 200 characters and the entered text ends with: “…favourite purple sock. It matters because it was o”
findings.why: The site accepted my action and advanced without warning that it had altered the core source memory, which will directly degrade the generated story.

findings.title: Truncation occurred after submission without feedback
findings.evidence: The typed 304-character value was accepted, but the box “only shows 200 characters” and the final sentence was cut off.
findings.why: There is no visible system-status message saying that the story was shortened, so the site appears to have worked normally when it did not preserve what I entered.

findings.title: Child-photo privacy handling is not disclosed before upload
findings.evidence: The page says “Upload a clear photo of your child's face” but provides no nearby statement about training use, retention, third-party processing, or deletion.
findings.why: This is my child’s biometric-adjacent personal data, and the site does not give me enough information to make an informed choice.

findings.title: File upload has no accessible label
findings.evidence: [30] is shown as “file-upload (no label)” while the visible control only says “Choose file” and “No file chosen.”
findings.why: An unlabelled native file control is harder to identify with assistive technology and gives the optional input no explicit context.

findings.title: Likeness claim is vague and unsupported
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.”
findings.why: I want to know what “look like them” means, especially because character consistency is the main quality issue I expect from this product.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” appear extremely faint in the footer, while [13] and [14] show that relevant policies are linked there.
findings.why: The privacy link is especially important before uploading a child’s photo, but it is difficult to see.

findings.title: Loading state has no text or stage information
findings.evidence: The central bordered panel contains only an animated circular spinner.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether it is generating the book, saving my truncated prompt, or stalled—especially after the earlier silent truncation and profile-sync error.

findings.title: No cancel or back control while waiting
findings.evidence: No Cancel, Back, or “work in background” control appears beside the spinner.
findings.why: I am trapped in an opaque state and cannot safely exercise browser navigation or recover if generation stalls.

findings.title: Footer and inactive elements have extremely low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are rendered in barely visible pale grey.
findings.why: Even the privacy link relevant to Zara’s data is difficult to find and read.

findings.title: Generated protagonist does not match the supplied appearance
findings.evidence: The supplied description was “Black hair in two puffs, purple glasses, astronaut hoodie,” but the cover depicts a generic short-haired figure with no glasses or hoodie.
findings.why: A personalised book where the named child does not look like the child is a fundamental failure, not a minor generation defect.

findings.title: Output style contradicts the selected style
findings.evidence: The preview states “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” while I selected watercolour on the look-and-feel step.
findings.why: It shows that my explicit presentation choice is not being honoured, undermining confidence in the rest of the generation pipeline.

findings.title: Generated title contains an obvious misspelling
findings.evidence: The title reads “The Magical Adventrue of Zara” twice.
findings.why: This looks unprofessional and is especially visible on a paid printed cover.

findings.title: The central memory objects are visually misunderstood
findings.evidence: The cover shows what looks like a house with a rocket attached, while a standalone purple “J” is presented instead of clearly depicting a purple sock used as a flag.
findings.why: The supplied cardboard rocket and favourite sock are central to our memory; generic or incorrect substitutes will make the book feel unlike us.

findings.title: Only whole-book regeneration is exposed and it is paid
findings.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
findings.why: If one page has a bad face, object, or line of text, I should be able to edit or regenerate that page rather than paying to reroll everything.

findings.title: Hardcover price is not shown beside the order action
findings.evidence: [9] “Order hardcover” is visible only below the fold, while [8] shows a $4.99 regeneration price without context.
findings.why: The prominent $4.99 can look like the book price, and I cannot compare print cost with regeneration cost from this view.

findings.title: Final-page sentence is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Zara looked up at the sky, they would always remember”
findings.why: The final sentence ends without stating what Zara remembers, so the book is visibly unfinished rather than polished.

findings.title: Zara is referred to as “they” despite supplied she/her pronouns
findings.evidence: “whenever Zara looked up at the sky, they would always remember”
findings.why: Zara is my daughter and uses she/her, so getting this wrong personally damages trust in the personalisation.

findings.title: Final image remains inconsistent with the requested style
findings.evidence: The cover and final image are flat, outlined vector-style illustrations despite watercolour being selected.
findings.why: The product has ignored an explicit presentation choice, so I cannot trust the style controls or pay $4.99 for regeneration based on vague claims.

findings.title: Footer legal and contact links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer labels “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” are rendered in extremely faint text against the white background.
findings.why: I can find the privacy information, but these are exactly the links I need when deciding whether to provide a child’s photo or purchase.

findings.title: Paid gift wrap is pre-selected by default
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox “Premium gift wrap” (checked), with “£7.99” added and “Total £45.97”.
findings.why: I would have to notice and remove an extra service I did not ask for; the default total is £7.99 higher than necessary.

findings.title: Shipping cost is not qualified by destination or service
findings.evidence: “Shipping & handling £12.99” is shown before an address has been entered.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether £12.99 is universal, a UK estimate, or one delivery tier, so I cannot judge the final landed cost confidently.

findings.title: Reservation countdown may create unnecessary urgency
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57” is presented prominently in red at the top.
findings.why: It pressures me before I have even reviewed delivery terms or decided whether the generated book is worth buying.

findings.title: Artificial reservation countdown lacks context
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:37”
findings.why: It creates pressure to buy, but I cannot tell whether the price genuinely changes, whether the timer resets, or what happens when it reaches zero.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The bottom links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” appear very faint against the white footer.
findings.why: The privacy and terms links are difficult to notice and read, particularly when I need to assess data handling before using the service.

findings.title: Child-photo retention period is undefined
findings.evidence: “Uploaded images may be retained to improve our services”
findings.why: Zara is seven, and an undefined retention period for her photograph means I cannot meaningfully control how long the image or derived data is kept.

findings.title: Secondary processing is vague
findings.evidence: “may be processed by our technology partners”
findings.why: I cannot assess a child’s data if the recipients, purposes, locations, and safeguards are unknown.

findings.title: Use for service improvement is not distinguished from model training
findings.evidence: “retained to improve our services”
findings.why: “Improve our services” could include human review, analytics, or model training. I would not upload a child’s image without an unambiguous prohibition or opt-in choice.

findings.title: No practical privacy rights or controls
findings.evidence: The notice contains no stated access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, or automated decision-making process.
findings.why: I expect direct controls to remove Zara’s photographs and generated derivatives, rather than only an email contact.

findings.title: The legal page conflates privacy and commercial terms
findings.evidence: The same page shows “# Privacy notice” and “## Terms,” with [7] “Terms” linking to /privacy.html#terms.
findings.why: A short commercial disclaimer attached to privacy information makes both subjects easier to skim and less trustworthy.

findings.title: Faulty-output liability is disclaimed too broadly
findings.evidence: “Digital previews are provided as-is.”
findings.why: A generated preview with a misspelled title, mismatched style, inconsistent character, and broken final sentence should not be treated as categorically exempt from correction or review.

findings.title: Low-contrast footer text
findings.evidence: The footer links “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear very faint against the white background.
findings.why: The legal and contact information is harder to read and the footer controls are less obviously interactive.
